content: 1. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor reduces the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable for effective birth control when used concurrently. Additionally, lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol through an unspecified mechanism. Concomitant use may increase the risk of menstrual-related adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 2. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Progestin and ethinylestradiol are substrates of CYP3A4, and systemic exposures to these hormones may be reduced, leading to contraceptive failure or breakthrough bleeding. Patients should use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction, such as an intrauterine system, or add nonhormonal contraception (e.g., condoms) during co-administration and for four months after the last mavacamten dose. 3. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of metyrapone through an unspecified mechanism, potentially leading to subtherapeutic responses. Discontinuation of estrogens, including oral contraceptives, may be advisable prior to and during metyrapone administration. 4. Mitotane decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable for effective birth control when co-administered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstrual-related adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 5. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided unless an alternative drug is used. 6. Mycophenolate reduces the effects of ethinylestradiol through an unknown mechanism. Patients should consider using an alternative or additional form of contraception. 7. Nelfinavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels, either increasing or decreasing them, which can reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 8. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 9. Omaveloxolone reduces the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives, including pills, patches, rings, implants, and progestin-only pills, due to weak CYP3A4 induction. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 10. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 11. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 12. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable for effective birth control when co-administered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstrual-related adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 13. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable for effective birth control when co-administered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstrual-related adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 14. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable for effective birth control when co-administered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstrual-related adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 15. Quinidine increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided unless an alternative drug is used. 16. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable for effective birth control when co-administered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstrual-related adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 17. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable for effective birth control when co-administered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstrual-related adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 18. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable for effective birth control when co-administered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstrual-related adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 19. Ritonavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels, either increasing or decreasing them, which can reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 20. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 21. Sugammadex sodium decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol by receptor binding competition. A sugammadex bolus dose is equivalent to missing doses of hormonal contraceptives. Patients must use additional nonhormonal contraception (e.g., condoms) for seven days after sugammadex administration. 22. Tipranavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels, either increasing or decreasing them, which can reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 23. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable for effective birth control when co-administered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstrual-related adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 24. Tovorafenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. If unavoidable, additional nonhormonal contraception is recommended during co-administration and for 28 days after discontinuation. 25. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A substrates according to product labeling. 26. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of albiglutide by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 27. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Atazanavir and norethindrone acetate may decrease each other’s effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 29. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by inhibiting metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Ethinylestradiol and aminocaproic acid may lead to additive hypercoagulability. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Amoxicillin and ampicillin may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of hormones. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Atorvastatin increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of bendamustine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
